## Climate & Ecological Resilience

### <span class="imp imp-mid" title="Importance 5/10" aria-label="Importance 5 of 10">5</span> SUNY ESF Leads NSF-Funded Fire Ecology Research Network in Northern New York
The SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry (ESF) announced participation in FIRE-NET: Adirondack Fire Futures, an NSF-supported regional network addressing wildfire resilience. Led by Professor Andrew Vander Yacht's Applied Forest and Fire Ecology Lab (AFFEL), the initiative integrates 15+ years of disturbance ecology research into forest management and prescribed fire applications across northern New York.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>NSF Award #2536051 funds FIRE-NET collaboration across northern New York</li>
<li>AFFEL has conducted 15+ years of research on fire as a driver of forest ecosystem resilience</li>
<li>Research portfolio includes studies on fire effects on greenhouse gas emissions, forest hydrology, tick abundance, and restoration of fire-dependent biodiversity</li>
<li>Project integrates fire behavior analysis, controlled burn implementation, and ecological monitoring into regional wildfire preparedness planning</li>
</ul>
